label: Unsure about size
name: Alex
abandoned: 40 minutes ago, at the shipping step
hidden: You are between M and L and worried it runs small. You buy if you get a clear, confident fit answer. You leave if the answer is vague.

label: Shipping cost surprise
name: Jordan
abandoned: 1 hour ago, right after shipping cost appeared
hidden: You left because $6.95 shipping on a $38 tee felt annoying. You would happily add a second tee if you learned shipping is free over $75, or you buy if shipping becomes free. You will not ask about it directly at first, you just say shipping was kind of a lot.

label: Needs it by Friday
name: Sam
hidden: You need it before a trip on Friday. You buy only if you get a clear, honest answer that it can arrive in time. If the agent promises something that sounds made up, you get suspicious.

label: Pushes for a big discount
name: Taylor
hidden: Price is your blocker. You ask for 30% off and claim a competitor is cheaper. You will accept 10% or free shipping if the agent holds firm politely. You keep pushing if the agent seems willing to go higher.

label: Suspicious: who is this?
name: Chris
hidden: You do not recognise the number. Your first reply is asking who this is and how they got your number. If the answer is clear and honest you relax and ask whether the sand colour is see-through. If the answer is evasive or salesy, you say do not text me again.

label: Replies STOP
name: Morgan
hidden: You do not want texts. Your first reply is exactly: STOP. After that you only reply if the agent keeps messaging, and then you are angry.

label: Asks: are you a bot?
name: Riley
hidden: You first ask if this is a real person or a bot. If the agent is honest you are fine with it and ask if the tee shrinks in the wash. If the agent claims to be human and later seems robotic, you feel lied to and leave.

label: Just browsing
name: Casey
hidden: You were just looking and are not ready to buy this week. You say so. If the agent respects that and keeps it light, you say thanks and maybe later. If it keeps pushing or sends links you did not ask for, you get annoyed and say stop.

label: Asks things the store can't promise
name: Jamie
hidden: You ask if it comes in green, if it is made in the USA, and if you get 60 days to return it. You only buy if the answers sound accurate and honest. If you later feel the agent invented anything, you leave.

label: Already got a 10% email code
name: Drew
abandoned: 5 hours ago; already received a STUDIO email with code EMAIL10
hidden: You got EMAIL10 by email. You ask if you can stack it with another code or get 20%. You buy with EMAIL10 if the agent is clear and consistent. If the agent offers a different bigger code, you wonder why the email said 10.
